facts.statement: Concavenator was a medium-sized carcharodontosaurian measuring about 5 to 6 meters in length and weighing between 320 and 400 kilograms.
facts.quote: Concavenator was a medium-sized carcharodontosaurian, reaching about 5 - 6 m in length and 320 - 400 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Unlike most of its relatives, Concavenator possessed tall neural spines on its last dorsal vertebrae that formed a sail-like structure.
facts.quote: Unlike most carcharodontosaurians, the neural spines of the last dorsal (back) vertebrae were tall, creating a sail-like structure.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalogued as MCCM-LH 6666, was described in 2010 by paleontologists Francisco Ortega, Fernando Escaso, and José Luis Sanz.
facts.quote: In 2010, the specimen was catalogued MCCM-LH 6666 and described by paleontologists Francisco Ortega, Fernando Escaso, and José Luis Sanz, used as the holotype for naming the new genus and species of carcharodontosaurid dinosaur Concavenator corcovatus.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen preserved integument traces, including scale impressions on the feet and tail.
facts.quote: This specimen was also found preserving integument traces, such as scale impressions on the feet and tail, which is characteristic of many of the lithographic limestones within La Huérguina Formation.

facts.statement: The skull of Concavenator measured 63 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Its skull was 63 cm in length.

facts.statement: The function of Concavenator's back crest is unknown, with hypotheses ranging from visual display to thermal regulation.
facts.quote: The function of such crests, however, is currently unknown. Paleontologist Roger Benson from the University of Cambridge speculated that one possibility is that "it is analogous to head-crests used in visual displays", but the Spanish scientists who discovered it noted it could also be a thermal regulator.

facts.statement: Concavenator possessed structures on its ulna resembling quill knobs, a feature previously known only in birds and feathered theropods.
facts.quote: Concavenator had structures resembling quill knobs on its ulna, a feature known only in birds and other feathered theropods, such as dromaeosaurids.

facts.statement: The interpretation that the bumps on Concavenator's ulna represent quill knobs remains controversial among experts.
facts.quote: However, the significance of the 'quill knobs' remains controversial, as some amount of skepticism has been raised among experts on the validity of the interpretation that the ulnar bumps represent quill knobs.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows Concavenator had broad rectangular scales on its tail underside, bird-like scutes on its feet, and plantar pads on the soles of its feet.
facts.quote: Extensive scale impressions were preserved on other portions of the body, including broad, rectangular scales on the underside of the tail, bird-like scutes on the feet, and plantar pads on the undersides of the feet.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses recovered Concavenator as an early-diverging member of the Carcharodontosauridae family.
facts.quote: In their 2022 description of the giganotosaurin Meraxes, Concavenator was recovered as an early-diverging member of the Carcharodontosauridae, in an unresolved polytomy with Eocarcharia, Lajasvenator, and Lusovenator.

facts.statement: Concavenator corcovatus lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian stage, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago in what is now Cuenca, Spain.
facts.quote: Concavenator corcovatus (lat. "cazador de Cuenca jorobado") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Concavenator de dinosaurio terópodo carcarodontosáurido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 130 y 125 millones de años, durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Cuenca, España.

facts.statement: Concavenator was a primitive carnosaurian dinosaur of medium size, approximately 6 meters long.
facts.quote: Concavenator era un dinosaurio carcarodontosáurido primitivo de tamaño medio, aproximadamente 6 metros de largo

facts.statement: Two extremely high vertebrae in front of the hips formed a high, narrow, and pointed crest that possibly supported a hump on the dinosaur's back.
facts.quote: Dos vértebras extremadamente altas delante de las caderas formaban una cresta alta pero estrecha y puntiaguda, posiblemente soportando una joroba en la espalda del dinosaurio

facts.statement: The skeleton features a series of small bumps on the ulnas and a small crest over the pelvis.
facts.quote: El esqueleto presenta una serie de pequeñas protuberancias en las ulnas, además de una pequeña cresta sobre la pelvis

facts.statement: Concavenator had nodule-like structures on its forearm, a feature known only in birds and other feathered theropods like Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Concavenator presentaba estructuras semejantes a nódulos en su antebrazo, una característica conocida sólo en las aves y otros terópodos con plumas, como Velociraptor

facts.statement: No skin impressions were found near the arm, though large-scale impressions were preserved elsewhere, including wide rectangular scales on the tail underside, bird-like scales on the feet, and plantar pads on the soles.
facts.quote: No se encontraron impresiones de ningún tipo de tegumento cerca del brazo, aunque se conservaron impresiones a gran escala en otras partes del cuerpo, incluidas escamas anchas y rectangulares en la parte inferior de la cola, escamas parecidos a las de los pájaros en los pies y almohadillas plantares en la parte inferior de los pies

facts.statement: The well-preserved fossil remains were discovered in 2003 at the Las Hoyas paleontological site in Cuenca province, Spain.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles están muy bien conservados, fueron descubiertos en 2003 en el yacimiento paleontológico de Las Hoyas, provincia de Cuenca, España

facts.statement: The fossils were found by paleontologists José Luis Sanz, Francisco Ortega, and Fernando Escaso from the Autonomous University of Madrid and the National Distance Education University.
facts.quote: por los paleontólogos José Luis Sanz, Francisco Ortega y Fernando Escaso de la Universidad Autónoma de Madrid y de la Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia

facts.statement: The description of this genus and species was published in 2010 in the journal Nature.
facts.quote: La descripción de este género y especie fue publicada en 2010 en la revista Nature

facts.statement: The specimen found in Las Hoyas is the most complete articulated dinosaur skeleton ever found in the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: El ejemplar de dinosaurio encontrado en Las Hoyas es también el esqueleto articulado de dinosaurio más completo que se ha encontrado hasta la fecha en la península ibérica

facts.statement: The function of the dorsal crest is currently unknown.
facts.quote: La función de tal cresta es actualmente desconocida

facts.statement: There is some skepticism among experts regarding the validity of the interpretation that the ulnar bumps represent feather anchors.
facts.quote: Hay cierto escepticismo entre los expertos acerca de la validez de la interpretación de que las protuberancias del cúbito representan anclaje de plumas

facts.statement: Darren Naish speculated that the nodules are too far apart and irregularly spaced to serve as feather anchors.
facts.quote: Darren Naish en Tetrapod Zoology especula que los nódulos están muy alejados entre sí y espaciados demasiado irregularmente como para ser el anclaje de plumas

facts.statement: Andrea Cau compared Concavenator's forearm to those of Allosaurus and Acrocanthosaurus, showing the specimen's forearm is dislocated and the ulnar bumps are on the anterior surface rather than the posterolateral surface.
facts.quote: Andrea Cau comparó el antebrazo de Concavenator con los antebrazos articulados de Allosaurus y Acrocanthosaurus y mostró que el antebrazo del espécimen está dislocado y los bultos cubitales están en la superficie anterior del cúbito y no en la superficie posterolateral

facts.statement: Cau concluded that the ulnar bumps likely formed part of a crest on the anterior side of the ulna, possibly for muscle insertion connecting the ulna and radius.
facts.quote: Concluyó que su interpretación era que los bultos cubitales formaban parte de la cresta en el lado anterior del cúbito, quizás para la inserción de la musculatura que conectaba el cúbito y el radio

facts.statement: Concavenator is classified as one of the most primitive members of the Carcharodontosauridae family.
facts.quote: Concavenator ha sido clasificado como uno de los miembros más primitivos de la familia Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Concavenator is more derived than its African ancestor Veterupristisaurus, indicating that Carcharodontosaurids were expanding to Europe by the early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Concavenator, más derivado que su antecesor africano Veterupristisaurus comprueba que ya a inicios del periodo Cretácico los carcarodontosáuridos se estaban expandiendo a otros continentes, en este caso a territorios de la actual Europa

facts.statement: Concavenator fossils were found at the Las Hoyas site, which dates to the Barremian period.
facts.quote: Los restos de Concavenator se encontraron en el yacimiento de Las Hoyas, datado del periodo Barremiense

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Concavenator lived in a wetland environment with lakes, ponds, and flooded soils containing aquatic plants, ferns, conifers, and early angiosperms, under a tropical or subtropical climate with dry seasons.
facts.quote: La evidencia fósil sugiere que Concavenator habitó en una zona de humedales conformado por una serie de lagos, charcas y suelos anegados habitados por diferentes plantas acuáticas, helechos, coníferas, e incluso algunas de las primeras angiospermas, con un clima tropical o subtropical marcado por períodos de estación seca

facts.statement: Concavenator lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Concavenator is Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Concavenator is Concavenator corcovatus.
facts.quote: Type species: Concavenator corcovatus

facts.statement: Concavenator is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The genus Concavenator was named by Ortega et al. in 2010.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Concavenator (genus), Ortega et al. 2010
